note: Published reference values used by the verification suite, each with its source. Values fetched by fetch_fixtures.py (JPL Horizons, JPL SSD) live in horizons_moons.json / jpl_sat_elem.json instead.

gm_durante2020.source: Durante, D. et al. (2020), Jupiter's gravity field halfway through the Juno mission, GRL 47, e2019GL086572; PDS model description 'The Durante2020 Gravity Field Model'

reference_radius_km.source: Durante2020 model description (reference radius); IAU 2015 Resolution B3 nominal equatorial radius (astropy.constants.R_jup)

J2_iess2018.source: Iess, L. et al. (2018), Measurement of Jupiter's asymmetric gravity field, Nature 555, 220-222 (unnormalized, R = 71,492 km), as tabulated in A&A 2019 (aa35938-19, Table 1)

J2_folkner2017.source: Folkner, W. M. et al. (2017), GRL 44, 4694-4700 (the game's own citation)

pole_iau2015.source: Archinal, B. A. et al. (2018), Report of the IAU Working Group on Cartographic Coordinates and Rotational Elements: 2015, Celest. Mech. Dyn. Astr. 130:22, Table 2

itu_r_p525_constant_db.source: ITU-R P.525-4 (2019), Calculation of free-space attenuation, eq. (4): L_bf = 32.4 + 20 log f(MHz) + 20 log d(km)

boltzmann_dbw_per_k_hz.source: 10 log10 k with k = 1.380649e-23 J/K, exact since the 2019 SI (CODATA 2018/2022): -228.599 dBW/K/Hz

kT0_dbm_per_hz_290K.source: Thermal noise floor k T0 at the reference temperature T0 = 290 K (ITU-R P.372-17 (08/2024) sec. 2, definitions under eq. (2)): -173.98 dBm/Hz

x_band_turnaround.source: CCSDS 401.0-B-32, Radio Frequency and Modulation Systems, Part 1, Rec. 2.6.2 (X-band up / X-band down turnaround ratio 880/749); DSN 810-005 Module 201

x_uplink_band_hz.source: DSN 810-005 Module 201 Rev. F (2022), Category B (deep space) X-band uplink 7145-7190 MHz; 7190-7235 is Category A

monopulse_slope_km.source: Barton, D. K. (2005), Radar System Analysis and Modeling (Artech House): angle-error σ = θ3/(km √(2 S/N)), km ≈ 1.6 a typical value for an amplitude-comparison monopulse (section not verified); readable corroboration: MIT Lincoln Laboratory, Introduction to Radar Systems, Tracking and Parameter Estimation (2008), slide EST&TRACK-27, accuracy ∝ beamwidth/√SNR

hpbw_tapered_deg_lambda_over_D.source: Balanis, C. A. (2016), Antenna Theory 4th ed., ch. 15: HPBW ≈ 70 λ/D degrees for a typically tapered paraboloid (58.9 for uniform illumination); readable corroboration: NAWCWD TP 8347 (2013) sec. 3-1, p. 3-1.1, BW = 70 λ/d
